# AllocError

Why an allocation, reallocation or release did not do what was asked.

```rux
pub enum AllocError: uint8 {
    Unsupported = 1,
    OutOfMemory = 2,
    InvalidBlock = 3
}
```

## Cases

| Name           | Value | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Unsupported`  | `1`   | The layout cannot be served by this allocator at all: an alignment stricter than it can give, or a size it could never hold. A different allocator might succeed; retrying with this one will not.               |
| `OutOfMemory`  | `2`   | The allocator has no storage left. A smaller request might succeed, and so might this one later.                                                                                                                 |
| `InvalidBlock` | `3`   | The arguments do not describe an allocation this allocator handed out — a pointer it did not give, or a layout that does not match the one it was given with. This is a caller's mistake rather than a shortage. |

## Methods

<h3 id="is-transient"><code>IsTransient</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsTransient(self) -> bool
```

Whether a later attempt could plausibly succeed.
`self` is borrowed. True only for `OutOfMemory`, which is a shortage rather than a mistake: `Unsupported` and
`InvalidBlock` describe the request rather than the moment, so repeating either gives the same answer.

**Returns**: whether asking again later could succeed

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Error.rux#L32)

## Related

<h3 id="allocation-failed"><code>AllocationFailed</code></h3>

```rux
pub func AllocationFailed(error: AllocError)
```

Terminates the program, reporting that an allocation was refused and why.
This is what an owning type does when the storage it needs cannot be had: running out of memory is not an error
its caller is expected to handle, and code that can recover calls the type's `Try*` operation instead. Does not
unwind, so no destructor runs.
A size that cannot be represented at all, such as a capacity whose byte count overflows, is reported as
`Unsupported`: no allocator could serve it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Error.rux#L46)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description               |
| ------- | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `error` | `AllocError` | why the allocator refused |
